title: Avery and Lewelling v. Nashville Presbytery
disposition_detail: As to actions taken November 10, 2015, the complaint was not timely under BCO 43-2 because it was filed February 23, 2016. As to the February 9, 2016 action, the complaint was not against an act or decision of a court but against activities of a presbytery committee, so it was not a proper complaint. All specifications were against committee actions and thus judicially out of order and unable to be put in order. The complaint was dismissed.
first_summary: Avery and Lewelling challenged Nashville Presbytery's denial of their complaint against the Shepherding Committee's investigation of TE Jim Bachmann and referral of its report to the Committee on Judicial Business. The SJC dismissed. It held the November 10, 2015 challenge untimely under BCO 43-2's 60-day filing period; the February 9, 2016 challenge was not against a court act or decision but committee activities. All specifications were judicially out of order and could not be put in order.
summary: Avery and Lewelling complained that Nashville Presbytery wrongly denied their complaint against Shepherding Committee actions: initiating an investigation of TE Jim Bachmann and forwarding the report to the Committee on Judicial Business. The SJC dismissed. The November 10, 2015 challenge was untimely under BCO 43-2's 60-day filing rule; the February 9, 2016 challenge was not a proper complaint because it targeted committee activities, not a court's act or decision. All specifications were judicially out of order and could not be put in order.
